title: Agent Foundry: A Platform for Building and Running Agent Systems
summary: Mark Norman presents Agent Foundry, a platform for building, running and managing agentic systems.

chapters.title: Where It Fits and the Responder Provider
Headless Claude Code and Standard I/O

learn: Agent Foundry grew out of Archipelago, his software engineering system, which is not yet fully autonomous; he pulled the shared machinery out into its own platform.
You compose structural primitives (loops, sequences, retry) and behavioral primitives, and any slot that takes one primitive takes any other; the primitives wrap LangGraph.

Agents are Claude Code running headless in containers and share Markdown files in a workspace. Clarification requests rise to the orchestration layer; the responder provider connects the running instance to the outside world over standard I/O.
Every run writes an artifacts folder, including a lifecycle JSON of agent, function and inference calls with timing, plus each agent's reasoning log, to learn from.
Archetype, which he plans to open source first, pairs Pydantic with Markdown to validate agent output and put the structure into the instructions. One of his biggest challenges is time.
